free_tier.stated: 5 GB of Standard-tier storage, 10,000 Class A requests (PUT, COPY, POST, LIST) and 100,000 Class B requests (GET, SELECT and all other) a month on every account; the allowance resets monthly, covers the Standard tier only and applies before anything is metered
free_tier.notes: storage is billed in binary GB (2^30 bytes) as the average of the daily peak over the month; DELETE and CANCEL requests are free

per_object_cap.stated: large objects up to 5 TB, under standard S3 multipart semantics
per_object_cap.notes: the page does not say whether 5 TB is decimal or binary

egress.terms: Free on every tier and location type: no charge for regional, region-to-region or internet egress, and no ratio or monthly cap is published; the pricing page asks for contact when bandwidth requirements are extraordinary. Reading Infrequent Access and Archive Instant Retrieval objects carries a retrieval fee, separate from egress.

tooling: All S3 SDKs, rclone, bucket forking, lifecycle rules, soft deletes
chaining: S3-compatible origin with no egress charge, usable behind a CDN or proxy front end; anonymous reads from a public bucket need payment-method verification on organisations created after 18 May 2026, so an account with no card keeps its buckets private.

limits.value: 5 GB of Standard storage, 10,000 Class A and 100,000 Class B requests a month free; above it Standard storage is USD 0.02 per GB-month

limits_note: Minimum storage duration: none on Standard, 30 days on Infrequent Access, 90 days on Archive and Archive Instant Retrieval; an object deleted, updated or transitioned earlier is billed for the full minimum, and one kept longer is billed for the days stored. Retrieval fee: USD 0.01 per GB on Infrequent Access, USD 0.03 per GB on Archive Instant Retrieval, free on Standard and Archive. An Archive object is restored before it is read: it moves to the Standard tier for a chosen duration and is billed at the Standard rate meanwhile. Storage is measured in binary GB (2^30 bytes).

identity_cost.detail: the console sign-in asks an email address and a password, or a Google or GitHub account; no card to start on the free allowance; a public bucket needs payment-method verification on organisations created after 18 May 2026; whether sign-up asks a phone number is unverified, as the sign-up link rendered the sign-in screen

reliability_note: Public-bucket access is gated by payment-method verification on organisations created after 18 May 2026, stated as an abuse control; no throttle is published, and extraordinary bandwidth leads to a contact request.
